quizzes.title: Governance Act practice set
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Governance Act and its rules mark a major change in how sports are run in India. The key institutional mechanisms came into force in January 2026, after the Union Government notified the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026. The reforms aim to make sports administration more transparent, inclusive and accountable. At the centre of the system is an apex regulatory body that decides which national sports bodies remain recognised, and it keeps a central register of those bodies. Elections in sports federations will be overseen by a panel drawn from experienced former election officials, so that long-standing problems of conflict of interest and factionalism can be addressed. Disputes about athlete selection, elections and governance will go to a separate tribunal, which is meant to resolve cases independently, speedily and at a reasonable cost. Doping-related matters follow a different legal route. Every national sports body must also have a general body and an executive committee; the general body must include sportspersons and the executive committee must include women. The reforms are meant to curb politicisation, arbitrary decisions and the lack of accountability in sports administration. Beyond governance, the government runs programmes that encourage fitness, identify young talent and support athletes who aim to win medals at the Olympics.

quizzes.title: Anti-doping and performance recall
quizzes.passage: Anti-doping rules in sport combine national law with international standards. A national agency under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports monitors doping control programmes across the country. India's standalone anti-doping law is designed to comply with the code of the World Anti-Doping Agency and gives authorities powers for search, seizure and disciplinary action. An international convention adopted by UNESCO urges nations to enact laws that eliminate drug use in sport, and it has been accepted by many countries, including India. When disagreements arise in the sports world, they can be taken to a specialised body that offers a fair and quick way to resolve them. Sport in India is also supported by government initiatives. The Fit India Movement encourages mass participation in fitness activities, while Khelo India identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels. The National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India. Indian athletes won several medals at the Paris Olympics and Paralympics, and young players have also made headlines in chess and shooting. In the years that followed, Congress asked Indians to observe 26 January as a day of national pride, and the date was marked in this way for many years. quizzes.title: Farm Safeguards and CBAM
quizzes.passage:
Agriculture is a sensitive area in the India-EU agreement. Under the agreement, duties on over 90% of bilateral trade have been removed, while sensitive items are handled separately. To protect rural livelihoods and domestic food security, both India and the European Union have maintained comprehensive negative lists for sensitive commodities. Products on these lists remain outside the tariff reduction framework, and the lists are meant to shield small-scale farmers from import surges.

Protection also extends to names and origins. A parallel agreement reinforces legal protection for geographical indications, preventing unauthorised use or imitation of iconic products in either market. Such a parallel agreement sits alongside the main trade terms.

Environmental rules form another strand. The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is an EU policy that imposes a carbon price on imports of selected goods from countries with less stringent climate regulations. India has viewed this measure as a possible form of green protectionism that could undermine export competitiveness. To support the transition, the European Union has promised financial and technical help for Indian industries seeking decarbonisation, and a Technical Cooperation Group will help exporters verify carbon footprints.

The agreement's safeguards therefore cover both agriculture and the environment. Together, these safeguards show how the agreement pairs market opening with protection for vulnerable sectors.

Negative lists are a feature of the India-EU agreement. Each side has listed sensitive farm goods that stay outside its tariff cuts, so that livelihoods and food security are protected. The lists are intended to keep small-scale farmers from sudden import surges.

Geographical indications also receive attention. A parallel agreement helps stop unauthorised use or imitation of iconic products in both markets.

The European Union's carbon border measure applies to selected imports, and importers must buy certificates tied to the emissions embedded in their goods. An earlier phase required only reporting, without any payment. India has been given an assurance on its treatment under the measure, and a cooperation group will help verify carbon footprints. Indian industries are also receiving European support for decarbonisation.

The mechanism is part of a wider climate package in the EU, aligned with its net-zero targets. It seeks to prevent carbon leakage, meaning companies relocating production to countries with weaker emission norms. Among its objectives is a level playing field, so that imported goods face a carbon cost comparable to EU-made products. Indian exporters also face stringent EU requirements for pesticide residues, certification and labelling. Data governance differences between the EU and India have also been noted.

India and the European Union have taken their ties beyond trade. Their joint strategic agenda aims to move the relationship from a mainly trade-oriented engagement into a multi-dimensional strategic partnership. It is meant to act as a structured action roadmap for a period marked by geopolitical uncertainty, economic fragmentation and rising protectionism.

The agenda is arranged into several pillars. The economic pillar centres on implementing the free trade agreement, while technology cooperation covers emerging areas and resilient supply chains. Defence cooperation is being reshaped, moving away from a simple buyer-seller relationship. Connectivity projects also feature in the plan. Cyber cooperation includes a partnership between the CBI and Europol. The EU's Global Gateway initiative is among the infrastructure efforts linked to the agenda.

The wider context matters. India is actively reducing its reliance on the US market, and the European market is presented as a stable, rules-based alternative. The agreement is described as reducing dependence on a single market. Space and cyber cooperation is also under way, including collaboration between ISRO and the European Space Agency. Joint research on advanced technologies is another area.

Cooperation on green transition and decarbonisation is also part of the agenda. The agenda builds on ties that have been developing for many years.

quizzes.passage: India's fisheries sector is part of the agriculture and allied sectors, and it makes a notable contribution to agricultural output. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was introduced as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package, with the aim of bringing a Blue Revolution through the sustainable and responsible development of fisheries. Its focus areas include modernising fisheries infrastructure, promoting sustainable aquaculture practices, improving post-harvest management, and enhancing the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers. A sub-scheme under it, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, supports micro and small enterprises operating in the sector and aims to formalise the sector under a national digital platform. The sector is also supported by integrated aqua parks, with parks planned in several states, and by a plan to develop climate resilient coastal fishermen villages. The scheme also aims to enhance fish production and productivity in India, to double farmers' income, and to coordinate fishery development in an integrated and holistic manner. A Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund also envisages the creation of fisheries infrastructure in both marine and inland fisheries.

quizzes.title: Rules 2026 and Sports Bodies
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 are meant to enhance transparency, inclusivity and accountability in sports administration in India. The Rules apply to national sports bodies, which include the national committees that oversee Olympic and Paralympic sports as well as the federations that govern particular sports at the national level. Under the Rules, every national sports body must have a General Body and an Executive Committee. The General Body must include sportspersons of outstanding merit, and a specified share of those sportspersons must be women. The Executive Committee must also include women members. The Rules set conditions that govern who may hold office in these bodies, and they limit how long a person can serve, using both a number of years and an upper age limit. Members therefore serve for a fixed period and must continue to meet the conditions laid down in the Rules. Taken together, the provisions are intended to make the governance of national sports bodies more transparent and accountable. The framework also includes a National Sports Board, which is described as the apex regulatory body for sports governance in India. The framework itself forms part of the National Sports Governance Act, whose key institutional mechanisms came into force from January 2026.

quizzes.title: National Sports Tribunal
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Tribunal was set up to resolve disputes in sport. Its stated purpose is to provide a forum that is independent and speedy. The Tribunal's functioning is linked to the wider framework of the National Sports Governance Act, which introduced several institutional mechanisms for sports administration in India. The Tribunal does not hear every type of dispute, because its jurisdiction is defined by the framework and certain categories of matters are kept outside it. Some matters that relate to sport are handled under separate laws and procedures, and the Tribunal's role must be understood in that context. The Tribunal has a defined structure, with a head and other members who bring relevant knowledge to its work. Its purpose, scope and structure together show how the framework seeks to bring clarity and order to the settlement of sports disputes in the country. The key institutional mechanisms of the Act came into force from January 2026. The Rules and mechanisms under the Act aim to enhance transparency, inclusivity and accountability in sports administration. The Tribunal is therefore one of several bodies created to strengthen sports administration in India. Its work is part of that framework and is expected to be read alongside the Rules that apply to national sports bodies.

quizzes.title: Tribunal Recall

The Tribunal's structure, purpose and scope show how the framework seeks to bring clarity to sports dispute resolution. A wide range of matters can reach it, but only those that fall within its defined areas. The framework as a whole is intended to improve how sports bodies are run, and the Tribunal is one of its key parts. The Tribunal's work is therefore closely connected with the other mechanisms introduced under the Act, which together form a single framework for sports governance in India.

quizzes.title: Pax Silica and Critical Minerals: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Critical minerals and advanced technology have become matters of strategic planning. A United States-led multilateral framework, Pax Silica, aims to build a secure, resilient and innovation-oriented global technology ecosystem, and India is set to join it. The framework is designed to counter vulnerabilities in critical technology supply chains and to reduce over-dependence on coercive or unreliable sources. Its key objectives include minimising strategic vulnerabilities arising from concentrated supply chains, safeguarding sensitive and emerging technologies from misuse, and promoting secure, interoperable and trusted technology networks among partner countries. Its scope covers semiconductors, AI infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, compute and data logistics. Within India, the National Critical Minerals Mission seeks to enhance domestic exploration, reduce import dependence and develop processing and recycling capabilities. The mission also encourages public sector and private companies to acquire mineral assets abroad, aims to enhance trade with resource-rich countries, and lists regulatory and financial support among its key objectives. A dedicated body, Khanij Bidesh India Ltd, is responsible for identifying and acquiring overseas assets related to critical minerals. Exploration is also extended to the Indian Ocean seabed under the Samudravaan Project, which is aimed at finding critical minerals there. The mission also lists processing and recycling capabilities and overseas mineral acquisitions among its key objectives.
